details.publicNotes:
A xenarian is an aeon of mathematical paradoxes, embodying those paradoxes' resolutions as they repair the space-time continuum. Much like fractrixes, xenarians are entwined with the fundamental concept of infinity and its finite manifestations within the confines of reality. But instead of being tasked with repairing spatial anomalies, xenarians concern themselves with anomalies that affect both space and time. They call upon fractrixes for aid in resolving complicated problems, including contending with anyone who would interfere with their vital work. They act with a cool, logical precision, their every action unfolding across multiple timelines in harmony. To witness a xenarian in motion is to observe the unraveling and reweaving of causality itself, as they prune divergent futures and stabilize fractured histories.

Aeons are caretakers of order and balance, who watch over reality and guard it from the excesses that would throw it astray. Those who seek to cause discord and chaos will find themselves at odds with aeons' goals.

Work is Never Done

Like most aeons, xenarians strive to maintain order and balance throughout the multiverse. They are frequently frustrated, however, as no matter how hard they toil, their work is only ever half finished. When the actions of meddlesome mortals result in further setbacks, xenarians often choose to simply eradicate the offenders rather than risk additional delays.

description.value: 100 feet. A xenarian can communicate mentally with any creatures in the aura using wordless psychic projections. items.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

description.value:
Frequency once per each creature's turn

Requirements The xenarian is at 1 Hit Point and would take damage

Effect The xenarian falls back on tiny fractions of their remaining Hit Point to remain conscious. They do not take damage.
160 feet. A creature that approaches the xenarian with a move action can't move more than half the remaining distance toward the xenarian. As a reminder, adjacent creatures are 5 feet apart.

Whenever a xenarian takes damage and is not at a damage threshold, the damage can't reduce them below their next damage threshold. When they regain Hit Points and are not at a damage threshold, they can't increase their Hit Points above their next damage threshold. Their damage thresholds are 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1. Even if a damaging effect deals damage of multiple types, such as a flaming weapon, or fires multiple attacks, such as a force barrage, all damage is first added together before the xenarian's Hit Points are reduced. If a xenarian has multiple types of persistent damage, they are also all added together first.

The xenarian recovers from the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, slowed, and stunned conditions at the end of their turn. They're also immune to penalties to their Speeds and the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} condition, and they ignore difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain.
A xenarian automatically detects and identifies space-altering magic (including teleportation effects) and time-altering magic and is only affected by the magic if they choose to be.

You and the targets are instantly transported to any location within range, as long as you can identify the location precisely both by its position relative to your starting position and by its appearance (or other identifying features). Incorrect knowledge of the location's appearance usually causes the spell to fail, but it could instead lead to teleporting to an unwanted location or some other unusual mishap determined by the GM. Teleport is not precise over great distances. The targets appear at a distance from the intended destination equal to roughly 1 percent of the total distance traveled, in a direction determined by the GM. For short journeys, this lack of precision is irrelevant, but for long distances this could be up to 1 mile.

Heightened (7th) You and the other targets can travel to any location within 1,000 miles.

Heightened (8th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on the same planet. If you travel more than 1,000 miles, you arrive only 10 miles off target.

Heightened (9th) You and the other targets can travel to any location on another planet within the same solar system. Assuming you have accurate knowledge of the location's position and appearance, you arrive on the new planet 100 miles off target.

Heightened (10th) As the 9th-rank version, but you and the other targets can travel to any planet within the same galaxy.

target.value: you and up to 4 targets touched, either willing creatures or objects roughly the size of a creature.

description.value:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

You repel effects that would hinder a creature or slow its movement. While under this spell's effect, the target ignores effects that would give them a circumstance penalty to Speed. When they attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} an effect that has them @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, they automatically succeed unless the effect is magical and of a higher rank than the unfettered movement spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.CdAyAiMGESvgNQtz]{Spell Effect: Unfettered Movement}

The xenarian reaches into the wells of essence that animate each creature in a @Template[type:burst|distance:20] within 500 feet and attempts to cut them in half. Creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:36] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Bisector for 1 hour.

Success The target's Hit Points are reduced to three-quarters of their current Hit Points (rounded up).

Failure The target's Hit Points are reduced to half of their current Hit Points (rounded up).

Critical Failure The target's Hit Points are reduced to one-quarter of their current Hit Points (rounded up).
The xenarian summons a fractrix to fight on their side assist in other tasks. They can Sustain the summon for up to 1 minute.
